Definitions, assumptions & source

Open the source workbook in SharePoint

  1. Source and freshness. Demand Planning _ Projects and Services.xlsx in the QE Team SharePoint folder. The header shows the embedded source modification time and reporting date. This standalone HTML is an offline snapshot; use Refresh data to import a newer workbook locally.
  2. Population. 19 named people. All seven filters support typing, search and multi-selection. Selected values are pinned at the top; no selection means all values. The timeline slicer mirrors Year, Quarter and Month, including Shift-click range selection. Region, role and person define the roster. Stream and work type filter demand but retain the selected roster’s full capacity; the resulting difference is not free capacity. The trend and heatmap show the selected year and quarter horizon for context and emphasize selected months.
  3. Capacity. Net monthly capacity comes from TransformedData Total Working Hrs - Break, after standard hours and Regional Holiday Hours. Capacity is counted once per person-month, never summed across project rows. The workbook supplies the regional baselines.
  4. PTO treatment. Public Holiday/PTO hours remain in demand, consistent with the Excel dashboard. They are not subtracted again from the capacity denominator. Accordingly, “actual utilization” here includes recorded leave, rather than measuring only productive work.
  5. Shared rows. All-NL and All-BLR entries are shown separately and excluded from individual utilization. Their interpretation (team total versus per-person hours) is unresolved. Eight repeated-header records with no hours are excluded from analytical views; all source records remain embedded. No hours are invented or multiplied across people.
  6. Arithmetic. Utilization = hours ÷ capacity. Capacity gap = capacity − plan (negative means a shortfall). Hours ratio = actual ÷ plan; absent denominator = unavailable. Person variance = actual − plan. Gross relief and headroom are summed per person-month. Transfer potential is limited to matched overload and headroom within the same month, avoiding offsets across different months. Period cards divide total selected hours by total person-month capacity. Period averages can conceal individual-month peaks.
  7. Missing versus zero. Blank hours contribute nothing to a sum, but remain blank in the record table and are reported in coverage. A numeric zero is a recorded zero. Having some actual hours for every person does not prove complete time recording. Past months are elapsed calendar periods, not confirmed accounting closure.
  8. Carry-forward scenario. Available for exactly one selected month with all work included. Sum max(prior-month plan − actual, 0) by person × selected percentage, added to this month’s plan. This is a sensitivity based on hours gaps, not observed backlog, project status, or proven remaining effort. Leave and other activities are included. Use only after confirming unfinished scope and avoiding double-counting with this month’s plan.
  9. Analyst assistant. The local assistant maps questions to calculation-based explanations for the current filters. It does not infer causal explanations or call a generative AI service. Suggested causes are hypotheses to verify. A live AI service requires a hosted backend and model connection, which are not configured.
  10. Actuals trend page. Each selected month is compared with its preceding calendar month using identical roster and work filters. With multiple months selected, the latest selected month is initially focused; month-pair buttons switch the detail. Change = current actual − previous actual. Percentage change uses previous actual as denominator; zero baselines and absent numeric records are labeled explicitly. Monthly actual utilization uses each month’s own capacity, and its change is expressed in percentage points. Actuals include selected leave. Daily records are unavailable, so matched month-to-date comparisons cannot be made.
  11. Interpretation. September is partial as of 20 Sep 2026; October–December are future periods. Future-dated actuals are flagged. Low future demand can reflect either a lighter workload or incomplete planning. Staffing and transfers require validation of skills, availability, deadlines and recording completeness. Hours alone do not establish delivery performance, productivity, or causality.
  12. Validation. Individual plan and actual totals reconcile to the source Dashboard’s eight-month trend; shared entries explain differences from raw TransformedData totals. No exact duplicate records or nonnumeric hour values were found. Each person-month capacity is consistent. Source rows are retained for audit and export.
